INVESTMENT POLICY OF EXAMPLE CITY

This investment policy is an administrative directive of the Finance Department.

Objectives: the City seeks to maximize yield consistent with prudent management, applying
the prudent investor rule and a total return orientation.

Strategy: a single strategy applicable to all funds addresses safety, liquidity, and yield.

Authorized investments: any investment authorized by the Public Funds Investment Act.

Maturity: the maximum average maturity of the portfolio is three years. For pooled funds
the weighted average maturity to reset shall not exceed 180 days.

Valuation: market value provided by the broker is used for reporting purposes.

Deposits and certificates of deposit: certificates of deposit from any bank are
authorized, insured up to the FDIC limit, and may be held by the placing broker. CDARS is
authorized without further condition. Municipal obligations rated investment grade are
authorized. Money market funds are authorized if any fund rated AAAm. Reverse repurchase
agreements may be rolled to manage carry. Pools are rated at the time of investment.

Settlement: securities transactions are settled on a delivery versus payment basis where
practical.

Ratings will be reviewed as needed and the Investment Officer may consider liquidation.
Existing investments are not required to be liquidated.

The Board delegates full responsibility for the investment program to the Investment
Officer. The broker list is maintained by the Investment Officer.

Certification should be obtained from brokers prior to transacting.

This policy will be reviewed periodically by staff.

Investment reports are provided upon request and reflect book value only. Investment
reports are reviewed internally by the Finance Director.
